hook_text: Two fourteen-year-old cousins, same family, same birthday month. One showers in a city flat, one fetches water from a communal tap.
clip_script: Palesa's morning: light switch, hot shower, supermarket cereal, a bus to school. Nomvula's morning: the communal tap, feeding the chickens, a forty-minute walk. Who has the higher standard of living? Count the stuff: Palesa's family has more income, electricity, internet and a clinic ten minutes away. That is standard of living, material well-being. But who has the better quality of life? Palesa's family pays big rent, sits in traffic and worries about crime. Nomvula's family owns its home, grows its maize, and the neighbours watch the kids. Quality of life counts what money cannot buy. And every January the long-distance taxis fill up with young people heading to the city: pushed by no jobs, pulled by hope. That is urbanisation.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of a city flat and a village homestead, each morning drawn step by step, then a long-distance taxi with arrows labelled push and pull.
mood: Warm and balanced, respecting both lifestyles.
pacing: Two quick parallel mornings, a pause on the big question, a brisk close on urbanisation.
